narrative.overview: MathQuest borrows its grammar from sneaker drops: every level owns a signature colourway and every game launches like a drop with a 3·2·1 countdown. The screens stay working screens; the world shows up through type, colourway fields, size-run mastery cells and the full-screen inversion on a right answer.
keyCharacteristics: One colourway per level, applied as a full-bleed field, never as a tint.
Ink on colourway, colourway on ink: two-tone pairs, no gradients.
A giant cropped level numeral as the signature on the home and chapter screens.
Mastery shown as four "size-run" cells: started, bronze, silver, gold.

rules.name: The One Colourway Rule
rules.body: A screen shows the colourway of exactly one level (or one colour per player in shared-screen modes).

rules.name: The Two-Tone Rule
rules.body: Colour pairs are ink on colourway or colourway on ink. No gradients, no tints, no glow.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number is set with tabular figures.

rules.name: The French Maths Rule
rules.body: Decimal comma, true minus sign, stacked fractions, non-breaking space before : ? ! ; =.

dos: Do give each level its colourway through --lv only.
Do keep targets at 48px or more and the keypad within thumb reach.
Do pair every right/wrong colour with an icon or a word.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion: the flash and countdown become static.
donts: Don't add gradients, glows, glass or drop shadows.
Don't use emoji as icons; icons are 24px stroked SVG at 2px.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading.
Don't let display type overlap the level numeral: fit it with --tw.
